## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Tang Esoteric ritual manual recorded (*jì* 記) by **Yīxíng** ([一行](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%80%E8%A1%8C)) — Śubhakarasiṃha's principal Chinese disciple and the systematiser of the *Mahāvairocana* commentarial tradition — for the **Buddha-Eye** (*Foyǎn / Buddha-locanā* 佛眼) practice. The Buddha-Eye practice centres on the goddess-emanation of Vairocana's mother (*Buddha-locanī mātā*) and provides a *yoga-tantra*-grade meditation framework integrated with the *Mahāvairocana-sūtra* ([KR6j0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0001)) Garbhadhātu mandala system.

**Abstract**

The text records a Buddha-Eye practice transmitted from Śubhakarasiṃha to Yīxíng during their joint translation period (716–727, ending with Yīxíng's death). The Buddha-Eye (*Buddha-locanā* / *Mahā-locanā* 大佛眼) is the visualised feminine principle of seeing-as-Vairocana, anchoring the Garbhadhātu mandala's central deity-family. The ritual presents the four-fold *yoga* practice (visualisation of the deity, *mantra*-recitation, *mudrā*-engagement, dedication-of-merit) as a meditative pathway to *darśana* of Vairocana's vision. The text became one of the principal foundations for the Japanese Shingon Buddha-Eye (*Butsugen* 佛眼) tradition, especially through the *Tendai-Esoteric* (Taimitsu) lineage of Annen ([安然](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E7%84%B6)) and Enchin ([圓珍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E7%8F%8D)). Yīxíng's "*jì*" attribution indicates oral-recording-and-redaction rather than translation in the strict sense — the standard mode for the Mahāvairocana commentarial corpus that Yīxíng compiled from Śubhakarasiṃha's lectures.
